knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Shift and Stretch Applied to an Exponential Growth Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087824/plots/shift-stretch-v3/534d07be96e8155f71a52387eeb57bd4c0e537a5a91ae6f5358f8a225024fedc.png)

The graph above shows $y=k({5}^{x})+c.$ Find the value of $k$ and $c.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k({5}^{x})+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-2,$ so $c=-2.$

Therefore, our function takes the form

$$
y=k({5}^{x})-2.
$$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ The labeled point on the graph is $(0,-1),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=-1$ into the function and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =k({5}^{x})-2 \\ -1 & =k({5}^{0})-2 \\ -1 & =k(1)-2 \\ -1 & =k-2 \\ 1 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k=1$ and $c=-2.$

The graph above shows $y=k({2}^{x})+c.$ Determine the values of $k$ and $c$ and find the equation of the curve.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k({2}^{x})+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=1.5,$ so $c=1.5.$

Therefore, our function takes the form

$$
y=k({2}^{x})+1.5.
$$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ Reading the calibrated grid, the marked point on the graph is $(0,4),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=4$ into the function and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =k({2}^{x})+1.5 \\ 4 & =k({2}^{0})+1.5 \\ 4 & =k(1)+1.5 \\ 4 & =k+1.5 \\ 2.5 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curve is $y=2.5({2}^{x})+1.5.$
